subject: Re: Empire Analytics — data governance RFI (hosted API)
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@empireanalytics.com>

Cc: security@empireanalytics.com

Subject: Empire Analytics RFI — hosted API data residency & retention questions

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for taking this. We have a few targeted questions as part of our security review for Redwood's hosted API. We're evaluating you as a vendor for our text-enrichment pipelines and need clarity on the following items so we can complete the questionnaire:

1) Data residency — where are request payloads and derived outputs stored (region mapping) and how is geographic routing determined?
2) Retention windows — default retention for request payloads, logs, embeddings, and billing metadata. Any separate retention for backups/snapshots?
3) Deletion process — what happens when a customer requests deletion of stored content? Timeline for soft delete vs hard delete, and whether anything remains in backups or long-term archives.
4) Evidence & attestation — can you provide a statement or artifact confirming deletion, and do you provide SOC2 / technical controls evidence for hosted customers?
5) Encryption & key management — who manages keys for hosted tenants? Are there options to bring your own key (BYOK) for hosted?

If you can provide a brief written response and any supporting attachments (matrix, short bullet summary) that would be great. We're on a tight procurement window — ideally by next Friday.

Appreciate it,

— Lena
VP Security, Empire Analytics
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@empireanalytics.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Empire Analytics RFI — hosted API data residency & retention questions

Lena — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise, actionable summary. I've attached a short residency matrix and a one-page retention summary (Residency-Matrix-Nov2026.xlsx and Redwood-Hosted-Retention-Summary.pdf). If you'd like, we can convert the deletion attestation into a signed letter once we reach contract.

1) Data residency (hosted API):
- Default routing: requests are routed to the nearest Redwood region by request origin (client region header or inferred by ingress). Regions we operate in (hosted): us-west, us-east, eu-west, apac-sin.
- What is stored where: request payloads and generated outputs are stored transiently in the region that handled the request. Control-plane metadata (tenant ID, billing records) may be replicated across regions for operational resilience — see attached matrix.
- Residency guarantees: hosted API provides best-effort locality. If strict jurisdictional guarantee is required (contractual region-lock), we recommend our Dedicated or Private deployment options (we can map single-region Dedicated pools per agreement).

2) Retention windows (defaults & options):
- Request payloads & generated outputs: default retention is 30 days for hosted API. This retention is configurable at the account level for enterprise customers via a policy (shorter retention can be requested).
- Embeddings / derived artifacts: stored for up to 90 days by default to allow for caching/feature reuse; can be purged on request.
- Audit and request logs (operational metadata): retained 365 days for incident investigation and compliance; log access is audited.
- Billing metadata: retained for 13 months to support invoicing and chargebacks.
- Backups / snapshots: system-level snapshots (for service continuity) are retained up to 90 days and do not contain long-term copies of customer-generated outputs beyond the configured retention windows.

3) Deletion process (hosted API):
- Customer deletion request (self-service or support request) initiates an immediate soft-delete of customer content in the active datastore; soft-deleted items are no longer readable via the API within 24 hours.
- Hard delete: we run a replication-aware purge that removes content from primary stores and then schedules background jobs to scrub replicas and caches; typical completion window for hard delete from all primary/replica stores is up to 72 hours, but residual copies in snapshots/backups may persist up to 30 days depending on snapshot rotation.
- For enterprise customers requiring guaranteed removal from backups within a contractually shorter window, we provide Dedicated/Private options and a separate deletion attestation process with defined SLAs.

4) Evidence & attestation:
- We can provide deletion confirmation emails and a deletion job id for each request. For contract customers we provide a formal attestation (letter) and can include deletion job logs for the event.
- Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II (available on request under NDA) and can provide an extract of relevant control mappings for hosted API.

5) Encryption & key management:
- Data at rest and in transit: all customer data is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest (AES-256).
- Key management: for standard hosted customers we use provider-managed KMS; for enterprise customers we offer a BYOK path on Dedicated/Private deployments. Hosted BYOK is available only under strict contract terms and involves provider integration; we can scope this if required.

Operational notes and mitigations:
- Caching: short-lived KV caches used to speed inference are ephemeral (TTL default 24 hours) and are not included in long-term backups.
- Access controls: strict RBAC for our control plane; tenant isolation at the serving layer and network segmentation for hosted service frontends.
- Incident procedures: we retain incident and access logs for 365 days and can provide scoped audit trails for deletion requests on a case-by-case basis.

Next steps: I attached the matrix and summary. If the answers above match what you need, we can: 1) provide a signed deletion attestation template, and 2) propose a mutual action plan to add contractual region-lock or BYOK as part of an enterprise addendum.

Best,

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Partnerships (Redwood Inference)

Quick clarification on backups and keys — left intentionally short so you can map into your questionnaire:

- Backups: snapshots are application-level service backups used for disaster recovery; we do not create separate long-term archives of customer payloads outside the configured retention windows. Snapshots may be encrypted with provider-managed keys in hosted.
- Keys: BYOK is supported on Dedicated/Private. For hosted BYOK requests, we evaluate on a case-by-case basis (requires contract addendum and co-signed operational runbook).

If Empire needs earlier deletion from snapshots as a contract term, we'll need to scope Dedicated/Private or an enterprise SLA with a shorter snapshot-retention rotation.

— Kimberly
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference
